## Analyzing College Majors, Earnings, and Employment in Maryland and Virginia

#### DATA 205 Capstone in Data Science

[![](images/Screenshot 2026-11-15 at 22.10.56.png)](https://www.axsource.com/blog/data-ingestion/)


### 1.load data & remove nas
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# Read the dataset
p1 <- read_csv("md.csv")

# View the dataset
View(p1)

# Keep college graduates with valid wages and majors
jobs1 <- p1 |>
  filter(
    !is.na(WAGP),
    !is.na(FOD1P),
    !is.na(SCHL),
    !is.na(SEX),
    SCHL == 21,
    WAGP > 0)

# Calculate median wage for each major
major_wage <- jobs1 |>
  group_by(FOD1P) |>
  summarise(
    median_wage = median(WAGP),# Calculate median wage
    sample_size = n()) |>  # Count people in each major
     
  filter(sample_size >= 10) |> # Remove very small groups
  arrange(desc(median_wage))  # Rank wages from high to low


# View the result
View(major_wage)

#2408 electrical engineering ,2417 naval architecture and marine engineering,
#3702 statistics and decision science, 2401 aerospace engineering ,
#2102 computer science ,2407 computer engineering,6204 operations logistics and E-commerce
#6212 management information systems and statistics



top_major_wage <- major_wage |>
  head(8) |>
  mutate(Major = case_when(
    FOD1P == 2408 ~ "Electrical Engineering",
    FOD1P == 2417 ~ "Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering",
    FOD1P == 3702 ~ "Statistics and Decision Science",
    FOD1P == 2401 ~ "Aerospace Engineering",
    FOD1P == 2102 ~ "Computer Science",
    FOD1P == 2407 ~ "Computer Engineering",
    FOD1P == 6204 ~ "Operations, Logistics and E-Commerce",
    FOD1P == 6212 ~ "Management Information Systems and Statistics"
  ))


View(top_major_wage)


```

### 


```{r}

# Read and combine the raw datasets
jobs_md <- read_csv("md.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
jobs_va <- read_csv("Virginia.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Apply common data cleaning
jobs_all <- bind_rows(jobs_md, jobs_va) |>
  mutate(
    STATE = as.character(STATE),
    FOD1P = as.character(FOD1P),
    SEX = as.character(SEX),
    ESR = as.character(ESR),
    SCHL = as.numeric(SCHL),
    AGEP = as.numeric(AGEP),
    WKHP = as.numeric(WKHP),
    WAGP = as.numeric(WAGP),

    State = case_when(
      STATE == "24" ~ "Maryland",
      STATE == "51" ~ "Virginia",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    Sex = case_when(
      SEX == "1" ~ "Male",
      SEX == "2" ~ "Female",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(State))
```


```{r}
# Create the lookup table for the eight selected majors
major_lookup <- tibble(
  FOD1P = c(
    "2417", "2401", "2408", "6212",
    "2102", "6204", "2407", "3702"
  ),
  Major = c(
    "Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering",
    "Aerospace Engineering",
    "Electrical Engineering",
    "Management Information Systems and Statistics",
    "Computer Science",
    "Operations, Logistics and E-Commerce",
    "Computer Engineering",
    "Statistics and Decision Science"
  )
)

# Prepare the common college-graduate wage dataset
college_wage_data <- jobs_all |>
  filter(
    SCHL >= 21,
    WAGP > 0,
    !is.na(FOD1P),
    !is.na(Sex)
  ) |>
  left_join(
    major_lookup,
    by = "FOD1P"
  )



```
